vault.group.settings.title: Group settings
vault.group.settings.order_help: Lower numbers appear higher in the vault list, among ungrouped vaults and other groups. Used when the list is sorted by Position.
vault.group.settings.grouped_vault_sort_: Independent from the global vault list sort. Position uses the grouped vaults list order (drag when sorted by Position).
vault.group.settings.grouped_vaults_help: Select vaults for this group. Vaults in another group are labeled and will move here when you save.
vault.group.settings.delete_help: Removes the group only. Vaults stay on disk. Hidden vaults stay hidden.
vault.group.settings.delete_confirm: Deleting this group does not delete its vaults. They stay on disk ungrouped. Hidden vaults stay hidden.
vault.group.settings.hidden: Hide this group in the list
vault.group.settings.hidden_help: The group and every vault in it disappear from the list, pickers, and Info until you show hidden vaults in system settings. Unhiding the group shows its vaults again.
vault.group.drop_to_ungroup: Drop here to remove from the group
vault.export.filename_sanitized: The filename was adjusted for this system: {filename}
vault.export.invalid_filename: This filename cannot be saved on this system.
vault.export.blocked_opening: Wait until this vault finishes its current work before exporting.

vault.rewrap.busy: A password or unlock RAM change is still running. Wait until it finishes before starting another.
vault.export.dialog.title: Export
vault.export.dialog.format_help: Choose a portable file. A .zip is an ordinary zip of the encrypted vault (no zip password). A .7z encrypts the files with 7-Zip — easier to open elsewhere, weaker against offline password guessing.
vault.export.dialog.zip_no_compression: No compression settings. This .zip only wraps already-encrypted vault data. Encrypted data barely shrinks, so the zip is stored without compression — faster, and almost the same size.
vault.export.dialog.seven_zip_password_h: Encrypts the portable .7z (7-Zip AES — weaker offline guessing than the vault). This must be the vault password so files can be decrypted. Use your vault password if you plan to import this file back into Upriv.
vault.export.option.store_zip_desc: + Ordinary .zip envelope of the encrypted vault — same Argon2id encryption as the vault (recommended). No zip password. − Unzipping does not decrypt; you still need Upriv and the password.
vault.export.option.seven_zip_desc: + Opens in 7-Zip / ZArchiver. − Weaker offline guessing than a .zip of the encrypted vault, and it does not save vault settings. This is not how the vault rests on disk.
vault.export.dialog.seven_zip_unavailabl: Portable .7z export is not available right now. Use a .zip of the encrypted vault instead.
vault.import.rename_prompt: The file name contains characters that cannot be used as a vault name. Choose a display name:
vault.create.title: New vault
vault.create.busy: A vault is still being created. Wait until it finishes before starting another.
vault.create.source_intro: Import a file or a folder, or create a new empty vault.
vault.create.option.import_desc: Choose a file or a folder. A Upriv vault .zip keeps that vault's settings. An ordinary .zip or .7z is unpacked into the new vault when Extract is on. Any other file is stored as that one file.
vault.create.option.import_7z_warn: The files are encrypted into the new vault. This .7z does not save vault settings. Display name, note, hint, unlock RAM, and the other options stay as you set them here.
vault.create.option.import_files_zip_not: This .zip is ordinary files. They will be encrypted into the new vault. Vault settings stay as you set them here.
vault.create.option.import_folder_note: The files in this folder, including subfolders, are encrypted into the new vault.
vault.create.option.import_folder_dot_no: Names that start with a dot may not be included. The folder listing does not always show them.
vault.create.extract_hint: Unpack the archive into the vault. Off stores the archive as one file.
vault.create.option.scratch_desc: Start with an empty vault and a new password.
vault.create.import_folder_unreadable: This folder could not be imported. Choose it again.
vault.create.identity_intro: Display name and optional note. You can change these later in vault settings.
vault.create.password_import_intro: Enter the file password and test it before continuing. Optional hint is stored in config only.
vault.create.password_import_copy_intro: This import copies ciphertext as-is. A password is not required. Optional hint is stored in config only.
vault.create.password_scratch_intro: Choose a new vault password. Optional hint is a reminder — never the password itself.
vault.create.password_files_intro: This .zip has no archive password. Choose the password for the new vault. Optional hint is a reminder — never the password itself.
vault.create.password_wrap_intro: Choose the password for the new vault. Optional hint is a reminder — never the password itself.
vault.create.general_intro: Idle auto-close, backups, and how much RAM opening this vault needs.
vault.create.advanced_intro: Optional expert settings. Defaults are safe for most users.
vault.create.settings_editable_later: These options and everything you set in earlier steps (name, password, hint, note, backups, etc.) can be changed later in vault settings.
vault.create.error.duplicate: A vault with this name already exists.
vault.create.error.source_missing: Choose how to create the vault.
vault.create.error.import_file_missing: Choose a file or a folder to import.
vault.create.error.password_not_validate: Test the file password before creating.
vault.create.error.import_probe_unavaila: Could not check this archive password.
vault.create.password_hint_help: Stored in plaintext in the vault folder — anyone with a copy can read it without the password. A short reminder only; never put the password here.
vault.create.note_help: Annotation for this vault (max {max} characters). Stored in plaintext in the vault folder and never encrypted — anyone with a copy can read it without the password. Do not put secrets here.
vault.create.group_intro: Optionally put this vault in a group. Membership (including a new group) is applied when you finish creating the vault.
vault.create.group_create_help: Leave empty to use the group above. If filled, the group is created when you finish — this vault is added then.
vault.create.error.group_missing: Choose a group, or leave the vault ungrouped.
vault.create.error.group_name_too_long: Group name is too long (max {max} characters).
vault.welcome_readme.intro: Welcome to your new Upriv vault. This note was created with the vault so it has something to show the first time you open it.
vault.welcome_readme.field.name: Name
vault.welcome_readme.tip.encrypted: Files in this vault are encrypted on disk. They are decrypted only in memory while the vault is open.
vault.welcome_readme.tip.close: Closing the vault locks it again.
vault.welcome_readme.tip.password: Your password cannot be recovered. If you forget it, the files in this vault are lost.
vault.welcome_readme.tip.hint: The password hint and the note are not secret. Anyone who can see the vault folder can read them.
vault.welcome_readme.footer: This note opens in {read} view. Switch to {code} to edit it, or delete it like any other file.
vault.change_password.success: Password changed. The vault body uses the new password.
vault.change_password.same_as_current: New password must be different from the current one.
vault.change_password.vault_open: Wait until this vault is closed before changing the password.
vault.change_kdf.same_as_current: Pick a different unlock RAM preset.
vault.change_kdf.vault_open: Wait until this vault is closed before changing unlock RAM.
vault.change_kdf.downgrade_warn: Lower RAM makes offline password guessing cheaper. Existing backups keep the old unlock cost.
vault.change_kdf.success: Unlock RAM changed. The vault uses the new unlock cost.

modal.file_manager.viewer.empty_body_tou: Choose a file in the tree to open it in a tab.

modal.file_manager.viewer.preview_unavai: “{name}” cannot be previewed in the browser yet. External editors will use the vault mount later.

modal.file_manager.unsaved.body: This file has unsaved changes. Save, discard, or cancel.
modal.file_manager.unsaved.workspace_bod: There are unsaved file changes. Save all, discard all, or cancel.
modal.file_manager.unsaved.close_vault_b: There are unsaved file changes. Save all, discard all, or cancel. The vault closes after that.
modal.file_manager.unsaved.close_all_bod: Open vaults have unsaved file changes. Save all, discard all, or cancel. Each open vault then joins the close queue, one at a time.
modal.file_manager.import_in_progress.bo: Files are still being stored in this vault. You can wait for the import to finish, or close the file manager and cancel files that have not been stored yet.
modal.file_manager.import_in_progress.cl: Files are still being stored in this vault. Wait for the import to finish, or cancel files that have not been stored yet and close the vault.

modal.backup.title: Backups
modal.backup.hint: Each backup keeps the password from when it was created. To use an old snapshot, create a new vault from that backup (does not replace this vault). Saves are never removed by retention; standard backups follow your keep-last setting.
modal.backup.load_failed: Could not load backups for this vault.
modal.backup.section.saves_help: Pinned snapshots — never deleted automatically when the vault closes.
modal.backup.section.standard_help: Rotated on close — older files are removed when you keep only the last N.
modal.backup.saves_empty: No saves yet. Use Back up now, or promote a standard backup to keep it forever.
modal.backup.backup_now_blocked: Available when this vault is closed and nothing else is running on it.
modal.backup.delete_confirm: Type the vault name, a space, and {count} to confirm:
modal.logs.title: Logs
modal.logs.hint: Plain-text diagnostic files from `.upriv/logs`. Deleting the active file makes the next write start a new one.
modal.settings.section.storage_intro: How files are stored while the vault is open. At rest both modes keep ciphertext in the encrypted vault. Encrypted directory uses a virtual folder (desktop) or in-app files (mobile). Upriv-plain writes readable files on disk while open — better for large vaults, less secure.
modal.settings.section.mount_intro: Each system has its own folder for this vault. The file manager folder applies on every system. Use the app folder follows System settings. Another folder is saved on this vault only. For an encrypted vault, that folder is how this computer's file manager opens the files: they stay in memory and appear there only while the vault is open and the switch is on. Plain text writes real files in the folder and ignores the switch.
modal.settings.field.mount.path_help: Use the app folder follows System settings. Its file manager folder is follow the app, on, or off, and starts as follow the app. Another folder is only for this vault and has its own switch, which starts off. Off leaves the open vault only in Upriv. On lets this computer's file manager open the files while the vault is open. Plain text writes real files in the folder and ignores the switch.
modal.settings.field.mount.inherit_desc: Follows the folder in System settings. If that choice is still no folder yet, nothing is created.
modal.settings.field.mount.custom_desc: A folder saved on this vault. The file manager folder below is what makes this vault appear there while it is open.
modal.settings.field.mount.plain_help: Open files are written in the folder this vault uses. Use the app folder follows System settings. Another folder is only for this vault. If System settings is still no folder yet, plain text has nowhere to write until you choose another folder.
modal.settings.field.mount.inherit_short: Follow the app uses the file manager folder in System settings. On or Off is only this vault. Off keeps the files in Upriv. On lets this computer's file manager open them while the vault is open. The files stay in memory. Plain text ignores this.
modal.settings.field.mount.shortcut_unse: Choose a folder in System settings first. Until then, this computer's file manager cannot open the vault.
modal.settings.field.mount.mount_help: Off leaves the open vault only in Upriv, so this computer's file manager cannot open it. On places a folder here while the vault is open, and the file manager can open those files. They stay in memory. Plain text writes real files here and ignores this.
modal.settings.field.mount.phone_help: This phone has no file manager folder. Use the app folder follows System settings. Another folder is where plain text for this vault is written on this phone.
modal.settings.field.mount.locked: Close this vault, or wait until it finishes opening, closing, exporting, backing up, a password change, or an unlock-RAM change, before changing this folder. Recovery is OK.
modal.settings.section.kdf_intro: Each option is how much RAM Argon2id uses to turn the password into a key. More RAM per guess makes offline parallel guessing harder, and every device needs that much free RAM to open the vault. Chosen at create; we never lower it automatically.
modal.settings.section.kdf_settings_intr: Unlock RAM lives in vault.header, not config.toml. Changing it verifies your password and rewrites vault.header plus the key wrap in the encrypted vault. The vault must be closed. Use Save in the footer after choosing a preset and entering the password.
modal.settings.area.password_save_confir: Change the vault password? The backup written now still uses the current password. Later backups use the new password.
modal.settings.area.kdf_save_confirm: Change unlock RAM? The backup written now still uses the current unlock RAM. Later backups use the new preset.
modal.settings.section.seven_zip_intro: Optional portable .7z export (weaker offline guessing than a .zip of the encrypted vault). This is not how the vault rests on disk — rest is always the encrypted vault.
modal.settings.save_confirm: Save changes to this vault? Some options apply on the next close or unlock.
modal.settings.change_password_help: Rewraps the vault key with the new password. Files stay as they are. This vault must be closed. A backup is written first and still opens with the current password. Later backups use the new password.
modal.settings.change_kdf_intro: Changes how much RAM unlock needs. Files stay as they are. This vault must be closed. A backup is written first and still opens with the current unlock RAM. Later backups use the new preset.
modal.settings.field.vault.display_name_: Rename only when this vault is closed or in recovery. Wait if it is opening, closing, creating, queued to open, exporting, backing up, changing its password, or changing unlock RAM.
modal.settings.field.vault.hidden: Hide this vault in the list
modal.settings.field.vault.hidden_help: Hidden vaults stay on disk but do not appear in the list, group pickers, or download until you show hidden vaults in system settings.
modal.settings.field.vault.hidden_locked: This vault is in a hidden group. Unhide the group first to change this.
modal.settings.field.vault.order_help: Lower numbers appear higher in the vault list.
modal.settings.field.vault.password_hint: Optional. Stored in plaintext in the vault folder — readable without unlocking. Shown at unlock. Never put the password here.
modal.settings.field.vault.note_help: Annotation (max {max} characters). Stored in plaintext and never encrypted — readable without the password. Do not put secrets here.
modal.settings.field.storage.mode_help: Encrypted directory vs plaintext-on-disk while open. Both rest as the encrypted vault after lock.
modal.settings.field.storage.mode_locked: Close this vault, or wait until it finishes opening, closing, exporting, backing up, a password change, or an unlock-RAM change, before changing storage mode. Recovery is OK.
modal.settings.field.backup.skip_unchang: A close writes a backup only when vault files differ from the last backup still on disk. Looking around, including file manager layout, is not a change.
modal.settings.field.auto_close.idle_min: The vault closes after this long with no activity inside Upriv. A notice appears 60 seconds before, or 30 seconds before when idle is 1 minute.
modal.settings.field.seven_zip.encrypt_f: Recommended. Names are hidden inside the .7z until you enter the password.
If disabled, anyone can list file and folder names in the .7z without the password — only the file contents stay encrypted.
modal.settings.field.kdf.import_package: This .zip already has Upriv ciphertext inside. Unlock RAM is stored in the vault header and is not chosen again on import.
modal.settings.option.storage.encrypted_: + Virtual folder (desktop) or in-app files (mobile); bytes on disk stay in the encrypted vault. Export a .zip of that ciphertext or a .7z when you need a file. − Needs a mount or in-app file manager while open.
modal.note.title: Note
modal.note.placeholder: Add a note for this vault…
modal.settings.danger_zone_help: Permanently removes this vault’s encrypted data on disk, config, and backups.
modal.settings.delete_only_closed: Delete is available when this vault is closed or waiting for recovery.
modal.settings.delete_confirm: Type the vault name to confirm:
modal.app_settings.title: System settings
modal.data_folder.title: Data folder
modal.data_folder.body: Choose where Upriv stores `.upriv/` — the folder that holds your vaults and app settings. Switching folders reloads preferences from that location; System settings only edit the active folder.
modal.data_folder.blocked_vault_activity: Close every vault that is open, opening, closing, or creating, and wait for any export, backup, password change, or unlock-RAM change, before changing or exporting the data folder. Vaults in recovery can stay as they are.
modal.data_folder.copy_hint: Keep a copy somewhere else. The data folder in use does not change.
modal.vault_root_gate.continue_confirm: Continue with this data folder choice?
modal.app_settings.section.language_intr: UI strings only; vault content is unchanged.
modal.app_settings.section.general_intro: App theme and the header overflow menu (⋯).
modal.app_settings.section.workspace_int: Each system has its own folder. Only this system can be changed. No folder yet is the start: nothing is created until you choose one. Next to the data folder creates workspace beside .upriv. Another folder creates workspace on the path you choose. The file manager folder starts off. While an encrypted vault is open, its files stay in memory. Turn it on and a folder appears inside workspace so this computer's file manager can open them. Off leaves them only in Upriv. Plain text writes real files in the folder and ignores it. Phones keep a folder for plain text and have no file manager folder.
modal.app_settings.field.workspace.path_: No folder yet leaves the location empty, so plain text has nowhere to put files. Next to the data folder creates workspace beside .upriv. Another folder creates workspace on the path you choose. Do not put that path inside .upriv.
modal.app_settings.field.workspace.unset: Nothing is created. Plain text needs a folder before files can be written to disk.
modal.app_settings.field.workspace.defau: Creates workspace beside .upriv. With the file manager folder on, each open encrypted vault appears inside it.
modal.app_settings.field.workspace.custo: Creates workspace on the path you choose.
modal.app_settings.field.workspace.mount: Choose a folder first. Off leaves an open encrypted vault only in Upriv, so this computer's file manager cannot open it. On places a folder inside workspace while the vault is open, and the file manager can open those files. They stay in memory. Plain text writes real files in the folder either way. A vault with its own folder appears at that folder's root and does not follow this switch.
modal.app_settings.field.workspace.drive: The file manager folder needs the WinFsp driver, and that driver is not installed.
modal.app_settings.field.workspace.fuse_: The file manager folder needs FUSE, and FUSE is not installed.
modal.app_settings.field.workspace.phone: This phone has no file manager folder. Choose a folder for plain text, or leave no folder yet.
modal.app_settings.field.workspace.other: Saved for that system. Change it there.
modal.app_settings.action.clear_workspac: Close open vaults before changing the workspace folder or the file manager folder.
modal.app_settings.section.vault_list_in: Toolbar buttons, row actions, and drag handles on the vault list.
modal.app_settings.field.show_hidden_vau: Hidden vaults and groups stay visible until you quit the app. Not written to saved settings.
modal.app_settings.field.always_show_hid: Saved in settings. Hidden vaults and groups appear in the list every time you open the app.
modal.app_settings.field.vault_list_show: Show drag handles on the vault list
Shows the grips used to drag vaults and groups up or down in the list. Turn off to hide them — list order and sorting are unchanged.
modal.app_settings.field.lifecycle_close: When on, the unlock dialog closes as soon as you confirm and progress continues on the vault row — useful when opening several vaults in a row. When off (default), the dialog stays open so you can fix a wrong password without opening it again.
modal.app_settings.field.lifecycle_open_: When on, unlocking a vault also opens the in-app file manager — only if no other dialog is already open. Off by default.
modal.app_settings.field.lifecycle_keep_: When on, time the computer is asleep or the phone has Upriv frozen does not count as inactivity. A vault that was already idle while Upriv was on screen still closes. Off by default.
modal.app_settings.field.file_manager_co: When on, deleting a file or folder in the file manager asks for confirmation. Off skips the prompt. You can also turn this off from the delete dialog.
modal.app_settings.field.vault_list_allo: Drop a vault onto a group to add it, or onto the list to take it out of a group. Turn off to keep drag for reordering only.
modal.app_settings.section.groups_intro: A new group is created only when you save. Leave the name empty to skip.
modal.app_settings.section.groups_settin: How vaults join groups from the list.
modal.app_settings.field.new_group_name_: Optional. Created on Save — not when you type the name.
modal.settings.field.group.new_name_help: Leave empty to keep the selection above. If filled, the group is created when you save this vault.
modal.app_settings.section.logging_intro: Diagnostic logs under `.upriv/logs` in your Upriv root folder.
modal.app_settings.section.hidden_vaults: Vaults and groups can be marked hidden in their settings. Choose when they appear in the list.
modal.app_settings.field.theme_help: Dark is the default. Theme applies when you save.
modal.app_settings.field.logging_enabled: Write app events to log files on disk.
modal.app_settings.field.logging_level_h: How much diagnostic detail to write. More detailed levels include the quieter ones.
modal.app_settings.field.logging_keep_la: Oldest archived log files are removed when this total is exceeded. The active file can add up to {perFile} more lines on top.
modal.app_settings.field.upriv_root_mode: Choose one way to locate your data. Only one mode applies at a time.
modal.app_settings.field.upriv_root_help: The folder that contains `.upriv/settings.toml`, `vaults/`, and logs. Optional mount parent is `[workspace].path` (often `<root>/workspace`). Each vault lives inside `vaults/<id>/`.
modal.app_settings.field.upriv_root_reme: Path remembered from `{file}`. Keep it, or choose another folder.

modal.help.title: Help
modal.help.hint: Short guides for Upriv. Search filters sections in the current language.
modal.help.body.overview.1: Upriv manages encrypted vaults. At rest each vault keeps ciphertext on disk (Argon2id + XChaCha20-Poly1305). You can copy that encrypted vault into an ordinary .zip (recommended) or export a portable .7z.
modal.help.body.overview.2: A vault is open (you edit files) or closed (encrypted on disk). The list shows the current state with a colored badge. Recovery appears if close did not finish cleanly.
modal.help.body.overview.3: By default, files stay encrypted on disk while the vault is open. On desktop you work through a virtual folder; on mobile, through the in-app file manager. Plaintext is not written to ordinary disk in the default mode.
modal.help.body.vault_list.1: The home screen lists every vault in your Upriv root folder. Use the sort menu to order by position, name, state, or last accessed.
modal.help.body.vault_list.2: The view menu switches how vaults are shown: default rows, large cards, compact rows, or block tiles. Sort and view preferences are remembered in system settings.
modal.help.body.vault_list.3: When sorted by position, drag the handle on a row to reorder vaults. Refresh reloads the vault list from disk. With more than one vault open, More options includes Close all vaults: each one joins the close queue. If there is unsaved text, a prompt saves or discards it and only then each vault joins that queue.
modal.help.body.open_close.1: Unlock asks for the vault password. While unlocking or locking, the row shows Opening or Closing with a time budget, and Backing up while the close backup is being written. Lock flushes the session into the encrypted vault using the open session — it does not ask for the password again. Plaintext-on-disk vaults ask you to confirm before wiping the folder.
modal.help.body.open_close.2: Lock always closes. Optional idle auto-close locks after inactivity.
modal.help.body.open_close.3: Export is a separate action: copy the encrypted vault into an ordinary .zip, or stream a portable .7z. This vault must be closed; other vaults can stay open.
modal.help.body.vault_settings.1: Open settings from a vault row gear menu: Preferences (name, storage, folder, idle auto-close, backups), Password, Unlock RAM, and Group (assign this vault). Compression for a portable .7z is chosen when you export.
modal.help.body.vault_settings.2: Save writes config.toml on disk. Some options apply on the next unlock or close. Change password re-wraps keys in the encrypted vault. The backup written for that change still uses the previous password. Later backups use the new password.
modal.help.body.backups.1: When enabled, Upriv can copy the encrypted vault into the backups folder on close. Each backup keeps the password from when it was created.
modal.help.body.backups.2: Open Backups from a vault row to list saves (never auto-deleted) and standard backups (rotated per keep-last), download, delete, or create a new vault from a backup (+ icon; that copy is the snapshot, so the source vault can stay open). Use Save on a standard backup to pin it. Deleting requires typing the vault id to confirm.
modal.help.body.system_settings.1: System settings (⋯ menu) control Language, General (theme, header ⋮), Vault list (toolbar and row buttons), Groups (dragging vaults into groups), logging, and hidden vaults. Language changes UI strings only — vault content is unchanged.
modal.help.body.system_settings.2: To copy a vault to another drive or machine, close it, then use Export on that vault’s row. Choose a .zip of the encrypted vault (recommended) or a .7z file. There is no bulk download of several vaults at once.
modal.help.body.data_folder.1: Data folder (⋯ menu) chooses where Upriv stores `.upriv/` — settings.toml, vaults/, and logs/. Mount parent (`[workspace].path`) is optional and not auto-created. It is not an individual vault. An installed app keeps the default folder in the account user-data directory. A portable copy keeps it beside the program. On Android the default folder is Documents/Upriv. The system screen opens on Documents, which already exists; confirm it and Upriv creates the Upriv folder inside. `.upriv/` is not stored in the app private folder.
modal.help.body.data_folder.2: Export a copy, the last choice in the Data folder window, saves the whole `.upriv/` as one zip, with every vault and backup. Vault files stay encrypted. Unzipped, it holds <name>/.upriv/, named like the file (upriv-<date> unless you change it): choose that folder in Data folder to use the copy. Every vault must be closed or in recovery while it runs.
modal.help.body.logs.1: View logs (⋯ menu) lists plain-text diagnostic files under `.upriv/logs`. Deleting the active file starts a new one automatically when logging continues.
modal.help.body.logs.2: Open a file to read parsed lines, or select entries to download a zip or delete old logs. Log level in system settings controls how much is written.
modal.help.body.security.1: Session keys live in RAM while a vault is open. The password string stays in RAM too after a successful unlock, until you quit the app or lock the vault. A wrong password or a dismissed attempt does not leave the password in that map. Passwords are never stored in settings files, browser storage, or log files.
modal.help.body.security.2: Encrypted directory is recommended: files stay encrypted on disk and you edit via a virtual mount or the in-app file manager. Plaintext mode writes real files while open. Previews, search indexes, Trash, backups, and app caches made while it is open can outlive the wipe. Full-disk encryption (BitLocker, FileVault, or LUKS) is what protects the disk after lock.
modal.help.body.security.3: The file manager folder decides who can open the files while the vault is open. Off keeps them in Upriv. On places a folder on this computer so the file manager and other apps can open those files. They stay in memory.
modal.help.body.recovery.1: If close did not finish, or the encrypted folder does not match the last finished close, the vault enters recovery instead of opening with no warning. For the default encrypted mode, unlock this encrypted vault again with your password. That opens the folder as it is now — a backup is not written over it.
modal.help.body.recovery.2: A plaintext vault that did not finish close keeps its folder. Remove the folder wipes it and leaves the vault closed. Files that were not saved into the encrypted vault are lost. A dead encrypted vault is restored from Backups or New vault, not from this dialog. A single corrupt file does not block the rest of the vault from opening.

modal.vault_root_repair.title: Repair Upriv data folder
modal.vault_root_repair.body: A `.upriv/` folder was found in the default data folder, but it is incomplete or invalid (for example a missing or corrupt `settings.toml`). Choose how to continue.
modal.vault_root_repair.rename_hint: Rename the broken folder to `.upriv-invalidated-…` so its files (vaults, logs) stay on disk, then create a fresh `.upriv/`. Your vaults will not appear in the list.
modal.vault_root_repair.delete_hint: Delete permanently removes the broken `.upriv/` and creates a new empty one. Vaults and settings inside it cannot be recovered.
modal.vault_root_repair.inspect_hint: Another option: check whether `settings.toml` or other files inside `.upriv/` are wrong or incomplete — fixing them may restore the folder without renaming or deleting.
modal.vault_root_repair.reset_settings_h: Write a new `settings.toml` with default preferences. Vaults, backups, groups, and logs in `.upriv/` stay as they are. This fixes a settings file emptied when a drive was unplugged during a save.
modal.vault_root_repair.choose_other_hin: Pick a different folder for a new `.upriv/`. The folder is checked first; if it is incomplete, choose how to repair it below before continuing.
modal.app_settings.upriv_root.switch_def: Continuing will create `.upriv/` in the default data folder. `{file}` will be marked inactive (path kept).

Continuing will repair the incomplete `.upriv/` in the default data folder. You can reset its settings and keep the vaults, rename it for safekeeping, or delete it. `{file}` will be marked inactive (path kept).

modal.app_settings.upriv_root.android_de: Continuing opens the system screen on Documents. Confirm the folder it shows — you do not need to open another one. Android grants Documents; Upriv creates Documents/Upriv inside it and keeps the vault there. Uninstalling Upriv leaves it in place.
modal.app_settings.option.upriv_root.def: Creates or uses `.upriv/` in Documents/Upriv. Confirm the Documents folder once. You do not browse to Upriv. Uninstalling Upriv leaves it in place.

Store `.upriv/` in another folder you choose. `{file}` remembers the folder. Uninstalling Upriv leaves that folder in place.

modal.settings.option.storage.upriv_plai: + Real files on disk while open (large vaults). Closed: encrypted vault only. Lock always closes and wipes the folder. − Unprotected while open. Close and delete cannot ensure the files are completely gone from the disk.
warning.upriv_plain: While this vault is open, its files are real files on disk. Anyone who can read that folder can read them. Previews, search, Trash, backups, and app caches made while it is open can remain after lock. Full-disk encryption (BitLocker, FileVault, or LUKS) protects the disk after lock. Lock saves the files into the encrypted vault and wipes them. Close and delete cannot ensure the files are completely gone from the disk.
plain.place.title: Where should the files go?
plain.place.body: This vault keeps files as real files while it is open. Choose a folder before unlocking. Nothing is written until you choose.
plain.place.default_desc: Next to the data folder. Later vaults that use the app folder open there too.
plain.place.custom_desc: A folder you choose. Later vaults that use the app folder open there too.
plain.place.vault_only_desc: A folder for this vault. System settings stay unset, so the next vault that needs a place asks again.
plain.place.workspace_locked: Another vault is open, so the shared workspace cannot change. Choose a folder for this vault only.
plain.place.class.removable: This folder is on a removable drive. Files can leave with that drive while the vault is open.
plain.place.class.network: This folder is on a network drive. Files can be read by whoever can reach that drive while the vault is open.
plain.place.class.cloud: This folder is in a synced or cloud folder. Copies can leave this computer while the vault is open.
plain.held.title: Files removed outside Upriv
plain.held.body: Other apps removed {count} files from the folder. They stay in the vault until you decide.
plain.close.kept: {name} is in recovery because {count} files could not be wiped.
plain.close.pinned: A backup from before these outside changes was kept.
modal.settings.field.seven_zip.compressi: How a portable .7z export is packed. Higher levels make a smaller file but take longer.
modal.settings.option.seven_zip.compress: + Fastest export. − Larger .7z (7-Zip copy mode, no compression).
+ Light compression. − Slightly slower than none.
+ Balanced size and speed. − Default when compressing.
+ Smallest .7z. − Slowest export on large vaults.
modal.settings.option.kdf.32mib_desc: + Lowest RAM here; needs 32 MiB to open. − Weakest offline guessing of these presets.
modal.settings.option.kdf.64mib_desc: + Needs 64 MiB to open. − Easier offline guessing than 128 MiB or the default.
modal.settings.option.kdf.128mib_desc: + Step between 64 MiB and the default; needs 128 MiB to open. − About half the guessing cost of 256 MiB.
modal.settings.option.kdf.256mib_desc: + Default. Needs 256 MiB to open. − Does not stop a weak password.
modal.settings.option.kdf.1gib_desc: + Needs 1 GiB to open; harder parallel guessing than 256 MiB. − Fails if the device cannot allocate 1 GiB.
modal.settings.option.kdf.2gib_desc: + Highest RAM here; needs 2 GiB to open. − Slowest unlock; fails if the device cannot allocate that RAM.
